### The ruling you are executing (triage, 2026-08-25T18:08:57Z — verbatim)

Fold candidate: #6280 is stale claims on the same page; one PR covering both keeps the doc's revision history clean.

⛔ **The fold is declined by this seat** — one card per agent. **#6280 is out of scope for you.** Do not touch the `check-doc-links` coverage claims; it is dispatched separately after your PR lands, and the reason is recorded on that card.

### ⚠️ Before your first edit to that file — this page has bitten three PRs today

`content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` was contended three times in R32, twice costing a rework round. **PR #6402 edits it and is in the merge queue right now.**

1. Create your worktree, then **`git fetch origin main`** and confirm PR #6402 has landed (`git log origin/main --oneline -- content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` should show it).
2. If it has not landed yet, **wait and re-check** before editing that file. ⛔ Do not edit a stale copy — that is exactly how PR #6398 ended up with a green pin run against a tree that no longer existed.
3. Branch from, or merge in, a `main` that contains #6402. ⛔ Never rebase, never force-push.

### The work — the snippet at `:1626-1637`

The page tells a contributor to *"Follow the existing pattern for pnpm + Turbo setup"* and then gives a block in which **every claim is false**:

| snippet says | measured reality |
|:--|:--|
| `actions/setup-node@v4` | `@v7` — 27 occurrences, no other version |
| `node-version: 20` | `'22.x'` everywhere (one spells it `'22'`) — and **20 is below the declared `engines.node` floor of 22.11** |
| `pnpm/action-setup@v4` | ⛔ **zero occurrences in the repo** — pnpm comes from `run: corepack enable` + root `packageManager: pnpm@10.31.0` |

⭐ **Ruled direction: replace the fossil with a pointer to one named current workflow as the living example**, keeping at most the two lines that never drift (checkout + corepack). Pick the named workflow deliberately and say why you picked it — it should be one that is small, stable, and actually representative of the setup a new workflow needs.

⚠️ **Re-measure all three rows on your own HEAD before writing anything.** The card's figures are from `090927f4f` this morning and the workflow set has changed since — PR #6402 added `docs-route-eager-closure.yml` today, so any count of `setup-node` occurrences has moved. ⛔ Do not copy the card's numbers into the page or the PR body.

⭐ And note what your own re-measurement will run into: the new workflow uses `corepack enable` + `setup-node@v7` + `node-version: '22.x'` and **no `pnpm install` at all**. If you cite occurrence counts, count them fresh.

### The page disagrees with itself — say which side wins

`:196` already states the truth (`Uses: Node 22.x, pnpm via corepack`) and **is** inventoried in the `doc-version-claims` ledger. ⚠️ If your rewrite introduces a version literal, the ledger governs it — check whether it needs a `KNOWN_CLAIMS` entry, and if you add one, anchor it to something re-measurable rather than to a number you typed. If you can write the replacement **without** a new version literal (a pointer to a named workflow does not need one), that is the better outcome — say which you did.

### Why nothing caught this, which tells you what not to rely on

The snippet is in a fenced block, and `doc-version-claims.test.ts` **skips fences by design**; `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` checks that every workflow file has a heading, **not** that the page's examples match the workflows. ⛔ So no gate will tell you your replacement is right. Your own measurement is the only check — show it.

### Constraints

- ⛔ **Worktree-first**: `git worktree add ../objectui-6308 -b claude/issue-6308-living-workflow-example main && cd ../objectui-6308 && pnpm install`.
- ⛔ **Never `git stash`** — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo.
- ⛔ **Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.**
- ⛔ Do not set `domain:*` or type labels; file findings **unassigned**.
- ⚠️ Run the **whole** `scripts/__tests__` tree, not a targeted subset. This page carries at least three separate pins (`ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`, `merge-queue-reporting.test.ts` per #4154, and the version-literal ledger), and a subset chosen from your own subject matter will miss the ones that fire on the page as a whole — that is what cost PR #6402 a round today.
- Changeset required. Open the PR as **draft**; this seat arms it.

### Reporting

Structured JSON report: the three rows re-measured on your HEAD with the commands, which named workflow you chose as the living example **and why**, whether your replacement introduced a version literal (and its ledger treatment if so), and the full-tree test counts.

## Review — ACCEPT (PR #6408). ⚠️ And a correction to this card's own explanation, which I wrote and which was wrong.

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R33.

### ⚠️ The correction first, because I asserted the false mechanism twice

This card's body says:

> Why nothing caught it: the snippet sits in a fenced block, and `scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts` **skips fences by design**

⛔ **That is false**, and I repeated it in the dispatch order as something the dev could rely on. The dev checked instead of taking it, and the file's own header says the opposite:

> *'Fences are SCANNED… the opposite of `check-doc-links.mjs`, on purpose'* — and the scan loop calls `collect()` on fenced lines too.

**The real reason none of the three lines was caught** is more specific, and it is the same defect family #6307 closed this afternoon — `SEP` cannot cross the text sitting between the toolchain name and the number:

| line | what breaks the match |
|:--|:--|
| `actions/setup-node@v4` | `@` between the toolchain word and the version — not in `SEP`'s class |
| `pnpm/action-setup@v4` | `/action-setup@` between `pnpm` and the version |
| `node-version: 20` | ⭐ the **literal word `version`** sits between `node` and `20` |

⚠️ Fencing was never the reason. I had a plausible mechanism that fit the symptom and I wrote it down as fact — the error this lane keeps naming and I keep committing. ⭐ The third row is a live blind spot rather than a curiosity, so I have filed it as **#6409**: `node-version: N` is how *every* workflow example in the docs spells a Node version, and the ledger cannot see any of them.

### The change itself

⭐ Ruled direction executed exactly: the fossil is gone, replaced by a pointer to **`readme-exports.yml`** as the living example — chosen because it is short, runs on every PR, and its setup is the complete pattern a new build/test/lint workflow needs. Only the two steps that do not drift with Node or pnpm stay quoted, and the page now says outright: *"Copy everything else — the Node version, the cache key, the install command — from the workflow itself, not from this page."*

⭐ **No new version literal introduced, so no `KNOWN_CLAIMS` entry was needed** — and it said so rather than adding one defensively. Given #6307 landed four ledger entries an hour earlier, the restraint is the right instinct: an entry that exists to satisfy a gate rather than to inventory a claim is worse than no entry.

All three rows re-measured on its own HEAD rather than inherited, and the count **moved**, which is why it mattered: `setup-node@v7` is now **28**, not the card's 27 — PR #6402 added `docs-route-eager-closure.yml` today. `node-version:` 27 × `'22.x'` + 1 × `'22'`; `pnpm/action-setup` still 0.

Sequencing honoured: it waited for PR #6402 to land on `origin/main` before editing the page (fast-forward, ⛔ no rebase or force-push). That page has now been contended four times today and this is the second consecutive PR to handle it before the collision rather than after.

### One residual I am recording rather than filing

⚠️ The quoted block still pins `actions/checkout@v7`, so it is a miniature of the fossil the card is about — it will drift when the action majors. ⛔ I am **not** requiring a change and **not** filing a card:

- the page's claim is correctly scoped — it says those two steps hold *"no matter which Node or pnpm version the repository is on"*, which is true, and does not claim immunity to the action's own major;
- the failure mode is mild: a reader copying `@v7` after the repo moves to `@v8` gets an older action that still works, unlike `node-version: 20`, which sat **below the `engines.node` floor** and would actively break;
- the surrounding sentence already tells the reader to copy from the workflow rather than the page.

Stating it so the next editor of that section knows it is a known, weighed residual and not an oversight.

### Verification

Full `scripts/__tests__` tree as instructed: **80 files / 2303 tests, exit 0**. ⭐ And a mid-run `console.error` banner (*"check-vi-mock-specifiers: the population COLLAPSED"*) correctly identified as an **assertion fixture deliberately exercising that failure message**, not a real failure — confirmed against the final summary rather than assumed either way. Doc gates over the edited page all clean; changeset present; control-byte self-scan clean.

### Disposition

⛔ Arming on **every** check green. CI is running on `54fc0c337`. Arms when clean.
